items.q: Where does unique purpose actually come from?
items.a: Not a personality quiz — **archaeology**. You are a **phenomenon**: DNA + early experience create a once-in-history combination. Purpose is a **life-task childhood seed** — a directional impulse visible early that parents, teachers, and practicality often bury.

items.q: When should you listen for purpose signals?
items.a: Around age **4–5**, inner signals about love/hate/gravitation. Gardner's **multiple intelligences** map the "grain in your brain." A clear life task then **funnels choices** so modern abundance doesn't paralyze you.

items.q: What accelerates learning more than rote study?
items.a: **Emotional engagement** — subjects that emotionally engage you produce faster plasticity (Greene's Paris French example: stakes and love beat rote). High **frustration/anxiety** can signal **wrong direction** — pay attention.
Use **patchwork mentorship**: remix many role models for different strengths; don't worship one flawed idol. Update influences as you grow.

items.q: How do you tell real transcendence from fake peaks?
items.a: **Real Sublime** reshapes self and purpose and **endures**. **False Sublime** (drugs, rage-scrolling, compulsive consumption) gives a temporary rush that fades and demands more.

items.q: What is "death ground" and why does it matter?
items.a: From Sun Tzu: being **backed into a corner**, where survival need unlocks **extraordinary energy**. Greene's stroke sharpened focus, gratitude, and willingness to act before "someday."

items.q: What should you optimize for when choosing a partner?
items.a: **Partner-value convergence** on deep values (animals, money philosophy, lifestyle energy) — not just house type or cuisine. Read **non-verbals**: words lie; micro-expressions, smile authenticity, and posture reveal character under stress.

items.q: How should you use AI without hollowing out your thinking?
items.a: Don't outsource **first-pass thinking**. Form your own view first; use AI to **augment** holistic thinking afterward. Creative anxiety means **push through iterations** until the work feels alive — not quit.
